summaryRaw: Hello, AmericaWhatever you need from government, start here.Describe what you needExample question: How do I get a passport for my child?Example 1 of 11: How do I get a passport for my child? It’s free to use, never includes ads, and keeps your privacy protected.29,000 websites into one.No more wandering from site to site. America.gov brings the government together in one place.See how it worksAmerica.gov keeps your data private.Your personal information isn’t collected or stored, and your conversation disappears when you leave.Learn about privacyClear answers. Official sources.Every answer is exclusively sourced from federal, state, and local websites.Learn about sourcesNo app to download.Just open America.gov in your browser on your phone, tablet, or computer.More coming in 2027Going beyond answers, you’ll be able to complete forms, track progress, and organize everything in one place.See what’s aheadFind federal jobs matched to your experience. The preview shows uploading a resume and comparing job matches, with details about the agency, location, salary, and remote work.Choose a campground. The preview shows a map and four campgrounds near Greer, Arizona, with photos and addresses.Compare medication costs. The preview shows adding Albuterol HFA and choosing its form, strength, and package size.Choose preferred pharmacies. The preview shows nearby pharmacies on a map, with their names, addresses, and selections.Update your legal name across agencies. The preview shows selecting Social Security, MyTravelGov, CBP Trusted Traveler Programs, and Global Entry / TSA PreCheck.Find housing. The preview shows a photo and address for Mocksville Place, a multifamily housing development in North Carolina.Apply for a passport and track its progress. The preview shows confirming a passport photo, submitting an application, and tracking it from submitted to processing with an estimated arrival date.Sign in to access services. The preview shows a Login button.

children.author: iamnothere
children.textRawHtml:
The usa.gov site is a good start, but it’s not really comprehensive, and I’m not sure it can be.

A few queries that I couldn’t find answers to through that site:

* How can you get a permit for a group event in a national forest?

* How can I become a federal contractor as a small business?

* Where do I go to get an amateur radio license and what are the steps involved?

* What are the requirements for purchasing tribal land?

Basically usa.gov seems to mainly exist for people following the “happy path”—go to school, get a job or run a simple business, get health insurance, buy a house, retire. It’s got a few exceptions for large minority groups. But the issue is that the total number of people deviating from that path is huge, even if they only need to find one thing that’s not on the path. Right now they rely on commercial search to get answers, which often leads them to scam sites or intermediaries who take a cut for filing paperwork.

children.author: goodmythical
children.textRawHtml:
Type "affordable housing", click "Contact your nearest public housing agency (PHA)"

It is less effort and requires less time than america.gov's:

Type "find affordable housing near me", wait praying for relevant results, recieve irrelevant results due to my rural isp having flaky geoip, told to click on the same link I already got grom usa.gov or one of three other irrelevant links or call this irrelevant phone number.

So my tax dollars are now funding a worse way to get worse results to people who can't use a well formatted site that they won't benefit from because they'll trust it implicitly despite it being demonstrably less reliable.

Brilliant.

children.author: mikepurvis
children.textRawHtml:
canada.ca is the Canadian government's equivalent, as far as a web 1.0-style portal/index into many other sites and resources.

Neither the UK or CA versions have "here's an LLM you can make general inquiries to" though; at least for now that appears to be unique to america.gov. Unclear to me why this required a separate domain with all this branding on it vs just being one of those "let our chatbot help you out!!!" popup widgets on the existing usa.gov.
